He snaps out of his shock when he thinks of his wife, who was outside when the raiding party arrived. He pleads for the player to help him find her - when players do, she is already dead. Pointed to her body, Benryn breaks down - the weight of guilt immediately crushing him. retrieved_synopses: Benryn is found trapped beneath a collapsed beam in a burning inn, coughing and frantic; the player can free him and he will follow until the party exits the blaze. Once outside he’s in shock at the slaughter—goblins and drow attacked the inn and bodies litter the courtyard—and he immediately panics about his wife, Miri, who’d been outside when the raiders struck. If the player locates her, she is already dead and Benryn collapses into grief, convinced her death is his fault after a petty argument about a dowry that drove her out. He’s distraught, pleading for help to find her and then begging for a moment alone with her body; the scene sits amid wider goblin/drow raids in the region, so nearby conflicts and refugees may be affecting the area off‑screen.

Finally, if the player finds his wife's body, he is heartbroken - he believes her death is his fault, because of a silly argument that they had.

He snaps out of his shock when he thinks of his wife, who was outside when the raiding party arrived. He pleads for the player to help him find her - when players do, she is already dead. Pointed to her body, Benryn breaks down - the weight of guilt immediately crushing him.

The Cult of the Absolute has ransacked the inn at Waukeen's Rest and kidnapped Duke Stelmane of Baldur's Gate. The player arrives after the carnage, finding corpses strewn about. The player casts 'Speak with Dead' on one of these corpses - a civilian that was caught in the middle. context: Benryn is found pinned beneath a collapsed beam inside a burning inn after a sudden goblin/drow raid; the courtyard outside is strewn with bodies and the region is in turmoil from similar attacks. If the player frees him (this can require a strength check — barbarians have advantage and failing twice can kill him), he joins the party until they exit the blaze. Once outside he’s in shock and immediately panics about his wife, Miri, who had stormed out during a petty argument; the player’s search reveals her dead. Pointed to her body, Benryn is devastated and convinced her death is his fault because of the dowry quarrel (the dowry was for her sister’s wedding), and he pleads for a moment alone.
